metadata.name: aera
metadata.description: Aera - overcollateralized COOK bank on Cookie Chain

accounts.name: share_mint
docs: The share token: aCOOK for the COOK reserve.
Unchecked and uninitialised here because Anchor's `init` for a mint
allocates exactly a bare mint, with no room for extensions. The handler
creates it, sizes it for MetadataPointer + TokenMetadata, and
initialises all three in order.
Token-2022 to initialise. It is never read as an account of any type.

accounts.name: liquidity_token_program
docs: Whatever program owns the liquidity mint. wCOOK and bCOOK are both
legacy SPL Token on Cookie; this does not assume it.

accounts.name: share_token_program
docs: Always Token-2022: the share mint carries extensions that legacy SPL
Token cannot hold.

instructions.name: set_params
docs: Tightening changes apply immediately; loosening changes queue behind the
timelock. `set_caps` is not a separate instruction — caps are part of
`ReserveConfig`, and cutting them is a tightening, so it lands instantly
through this same path.

instructions.name: init_market_oracle
docs: Create or change a reserve's per-wallet borrow cap.
Lives in its own account rather than on `ReserveConfig`: growing
`Reserve` would leave older reserves undeserialisable to this program,
which breaks `accrue`, which breaks repayment for a whole migration.
`migrate.rs:145` records that being tried and caught.
Attach pools and thresholds to a `MarketTwap` oracle.

accounts.name: market_oracle
docs: Permissionless, like every other `apply_pending_*`: the delay is the
control, and the change was authorised when it was queued.

instructions.name: refresh_market_oracle
docs: Derive a market price from two AMM pools and append it to the history.
**Permissionless.** The caller supplies no price -- they hand over pool
accounts and the program reads the reserves itself. There is nothing to
lie about, so there is no privilege to hold, and Aera does not become a
liveness monopoly for the markets that use it.

accounts.name: pool_b_amm_program_data
docs: both pools are on one AMM, which a read-only account may be.

instructions.name: set_risk_config
docs: Set the reserve's per-wallet borrow cap and Aera's share of its
liquidation bonus.
Both in one instruction because both live in one account and both follow
the same tightening/loosening rule. `protocol_liquidation_share_bps` is
carved out of the reserve's existing `liquidation_bonus_bps` and never
added to it, so raising it cannot increase a borrower's penalty.

instructions.name: set_share_metadata
docs: Rewrite a share token's name, symbol and URI.
Not timelocked, and deliberately so: these three fields decide what a
wallet draws beside a balance and nothing about what the protocol
enforces. There is no position whose value this can move. The URI is also
the one field certain to rot -- it names a host, and hosts move -- which
is why leaving it immutable was a mistake worth an upgrade to correct.

instructions.name: set_oracle
docs: Configure where an asset's rate is derived from, and the bounds it must
stay inside. Never the rate itself -- there is no instruction in this
program that accepts one.

accounts.name: mint
docs: as the mint the source must issue; it is never deserialized here.

instructions.name: refresh_oracle
docs: Re-derive the rate from its source and judge it against the breaker.
Permissionless: the caller supplies nothing and cannot influence the
result.

instructions.name: reset_oracle_breaker
docs: Clear a breaker freeze by re-anchoring to whatever the source currently
reports. The admin chooses when, never what.

instructions.name: migrate_reserve_to_v2
docs: Move one reserve off the guardian feed and onto the derived oracle.
Send one per reserve in a single transaction. Atomic per reserve, and
it asserts on chain that no economic field moved.

accounts.name: global
docs: a v0.1 `Global` is one byte short of the v0.2 struct, so
`Account<Global>` cannot deserialize the very state being migrated. The
discriminator and the admin are checked by hand in the handler.
This is why the version stamp is a separate instruction and goes last:
if `Global` were migrated first, every reserve migration would need to
handle both shapes instead of only the old one.

accounts.name: legacy_price_feed
docs: it is validated by address, owner and discriminator in the handler and
closed by hand there -- Anchor's `close` needs a typed account, and
there is no type left to give it. Its contents are guardian submissions
and are deliberately not read; see the module docs.

accounts.name: liquidity_mint
docs: must issue.

instructions.name: migrate_global_to_v2
docs: Stamp the protocol version. Last, after every reserve has migrated.

accounts.name: global
docs: deserialize, which is precisely the state being migrated. Discriminator,
admin and length are all checked by hand in the handler.

accounts.name: supply_position
docs: Created on first supply. Exists only to make the per-wallet cap a
program rule.

accounts.name: share_token_program
docs: Always Token-2022: the share mint carries metadata extensions.

accounts.name: share_token_program
docs: Always Token-2022: the share mint carries metadata extensions.

accounts.name: share_token_program
docs: Shares are Token-2022; collateral only ever moves share tokens.

accounts.name: share_token_program
docs: Shares are Token-2022; collateral only ever moves share tokens.

accounts.name: risk_config
docs: The reserve's risk limits, which may not exist.
**Required, not `Option`.** An `Option<Account<..>>` is omittable by the
caller, so a borrower could evade the cap simply by not passing it. This
account must always be supplied; when the reserve has no limits the
caller passes the derived address of an account that was never created,
and the handler reads it as unlimited.
It cannot be substituted either: the handler derives the expected address
from this reserve and refuses anything else, so a RiskConfig belonging to
a different reserve is rejected.
It lives beside the reserve rather than inside it because `Reserve` could
not grow -- `migrate.rs:145` records that a longer `Reserve` leaves older
accounts undeserialisable, which breaks `accrue`, which breaks repayment
for the whole migration window.

instructions.name: absorb_bad_debt
docs: Recognise debt that no collateral stands behind.
Permissionless, because the precondition is verifiable on chain and the
effect only ever reduces what the protocol claims to hold. See
`instructions::absorb_bad_debt` for who absorbs the loss.

accounts.name: global
docs: Read only, and never a gate: liquidation ignores `paused` exactly as it
did before. It is here so Aera's share can be checked against
`fee_destination`.

accounts.name: collateral_risk_config
docs: The collateral reserve's risk limits, carrying Aera's share of the
liquidation bonus. Follows `borrow`'s pattern exactly: **required, not
`Option`**, because an `Option` is omittable and a liquidator could then
keep Aera's share simply by leaving it out. A reserve with no limits is
addressed by its derived-but-uncreated PDA and reads as a zero share.

accounts.name: protocol_collateral_dest
docs: Where Aera's share goes: a token account for this collateral's share
mint, owned by `global.fee_destination`.
Unchecked rather than typed on purpose. A typed account is deserialised
on every call, so a liquidation of a reserve that owes Aera nothing would
start depending on a fee account existing and being well-formed.
Liquidation is the last operation that should acquire a new way to fail.
`mut` because it receives a transfer. That marks it writable and nothing
more -- who may be written to is decided entirely by the checks in the
handler, which pin both the mint and the authority.

accounts.name: share_token_program
docs: The seized collateral is a share token, so Token-2022.

instructions.name: init_isolated_config
docs: Aera's policy for creator markets: quote asset, allowed AMMs, creation
fee, on/off. Admin, once.

accounts.name: quote_mint
docs: The quote asset of every creator market (bridged SOL). Fixed forever.

instructions.name: set_isolated_config
docs: Change the creation fee (bounded), the AMM allowlist, or switch new
creation off. Never touches an existing market.

instructions.name: apply_isolated_amms
docs: Apply a queued AMM allowlist after its fixed delay. Permissionless.

instructions.name: refresh_isolated_oracle
docs: The creator-market oracle refresh. Permissionless. Records a sample only
from a transaction that does nothing else; see
`instructions::isolated::oracle`.

accounts.name: pool_a
docs: `read_isolated_pool`: a wrong address is an error, a pinned account
that no longer reads as a pool is a degradation.

accounts.name: pool_a_amm_program_data
docs: degrades.

instructions.name: create_isolated_market
docs: Create a market for any token. **Permissionless.** The creator picks a
tier, one or two pools on allowed AMMs, and a bond; the tier table picks
everything else.

accounts.name: market
docs: The id comes from the config's counter, so a creator cannot choose it,
and `init_market` refuses this range, so the admin cannot either.

accounts.name: token_mint
docs: `validate_listing_mint` before anything is priced against it.

accounts.name: isolated_oracle
docs: At the address a `MarketOracle` would take, so no admin-market oracle
instruction can be pointed at a creator oracle. See `IsolatedOracle`.

accounts.name: bond_vault
docs: The bond. Owned by the isolated-market PDA, so only this program's
bond rules can move it.

accounts.name: fee_destination_quote
docs: Aera's quote account: owned by `Global::fee_destination`, like every
other fee Aera takes.

accounts.name: pool_a
docs: allowlist; any failure refuses creation.

accounts.name: risk_config
docs: The per-wallet borrow cap lives here, as on every reserve that has one,
so `borrow` enforces it with no change.

instructions.name: harvest_creator_fees
docs: Mint the creator their cut of lender interest. Permissionless.

accounts.name: creator_share
docs: Only ever the creator's own account for this share mint.

instructions.name: freeze_isolated_market
docs: Aera's kill switch for one creator market: new borrowing only.

instructions.name: retire_isolated_market
docs: The creator stops new borrowing for good.

instructions.name: withdraw_bond
docs: Only bond that outstanding debt does not need.

instructions.name: sync_isolated_caps
docs: Re-measure depth from the oracle's own history. Permissionless.

instructions.name: sync_isolated_amm_pins
docs: Copy an admin-approved AMM re-pin into one market. Permissionless.

instructions.name: cover_isolated_debt
docs: The bond repays a loan nobody else will. Permissionless.

accounts.name: obligation_collateral_vault
docs: address is derived and checked in the handler, and it is only touched
when the obligation holds collateral -- a borrower who never deposited
has no such account, and case A must still be callable for them.

accounts.name: creator_collateral_dest
docs: program are checked in the handler, and only when collateral moves.

types.name: OracleConfig
docs: Everything an admin may choose about an oracle.
A struct rather than a long argument list so adding a bound later is a
serialization change in one place, and so the timelock logic in `set_params`
can compare an old and a new configuration field by field.

fields.name: source_kind
docs: [`crate::oracle::OracleSourceKind`] as `u8`.

fields.name: source_program
docs: Program that must own `source_account`. Zero for `UnitOfAccount`.

fields.name: source_account
docs: The account the rate is derived from. Zero for `UnitOfAccount`.

fields.name: max_withdrawal_fee_bps
docs: Redemption fee past which observations are refused.

fields.name: expected_deploy_slot
docs: The source program's `ProgramData` deploy slot at the moment this
configuration was authorised.
An admin choosing this is not choosing a price: they are recording which
deployment of somebody else's program they reviewed. If that program is
redeployed the slot moves, every observation is refused, and borrowing
freezes until a human looks at the new code and re-authorises it.

fields.name: expected_upgrade_authority
docs: The source program's upgrade authority at that moment, or all zeros if
it was already immutable.

types.name: ShareMetadata
docs: Name, symbol and URI for a reserve's share token.
Passed in rather than derived so the COOK reserve can mint "Aera COOK"
(`aCOOK`) and a second reserve can carry its own identity, without the
program shipping a table of strings it would have to be upgraded to change.

types.name: PoolChoice
docs: A pool the creator names, and which allowed AMM it claims to be on.
The AMM's program, `ProgramData` and deploy slot come from
`IsolatedConfig.amms[amm_index]`, never from the creator.

types.name: BreakerConfig
docs: Breaker bounds. Held in `OracleState` so a second market could be tuned
differently, and so tests can drive the boundaries directly.

fields.name: max_up_bps_per_epoch
docs: Maximum upward move per elapsed pool epoch, in basis points.

fields.name: max_down_bps_per_epoch
docs: Maximum downward move per elapsed pool epoch, in basis points.

fields.name: emergency_deviation_bps
docs: Absolute move from the reference, in either direction, that goes
straight to `Emergency` regardless of how long has elapsed.

fields.name: max_epoch_allowance
docs: Ceiling on how many epochs of allowance may accumulate. Without it, a
reference left un-refreshed for a year would permit an unbounded jump.

types.name: Reference
docs: The last observation the breaker accepted. This is the protocol's anchor.

fields.name: source_epoch
docs: The source's own epoch marker at the moment of acceptance. Movement is
measured per elapsed epoch against this, not against wall clock.

fields.name: admin
docs: The only key that may create markets/reserves, change parameters, or
pause. Rotating it is a deliberate, separate instruction.

fields.name: fee_destination
docs: Where the protocol's whole cut of interest is paid.
One destination, not two: the reserve factor accrues 100% here. A split
would have to be reconciled at every accrual and every payout, and there
is no second beneficiary to reconcile it for.

fields.name: paused
docs: Blocks every state-changing user instruction except `repay`. Repay is
never blocked: refusing repayment while prices move would manufacture
liquidations the borrower could have avoided.

fields.name: borrow_paused
docs: Blocks new borrows only. Supply, withdraw, repay and liquidate continue.
Set by the admin, and independently by the oracle circuit breaker.

fields.name: param_timelock_seconds
docs: Delay applied to *loosening* parameter changes. Tightening changes and
pauses bypass it entirely.

fields.name: version
docs: Schema version. Absent in v0.1, so a v0.1 account is exactly one byte
shorter than this struct and reads as [`GLOBAL_VERSION_V1`] once
realloc'd and zero-filled.
Declared last on purpose: appending keeps every preceding field at the
offset it already occupies, so the realloc adds a byte rather than
moving anything.

types.name: AmmPin
docs: One AMM creator markets may price from, as reviewed by Aera.
A creator chooses which allowed AMM each of their pools is on, never the
AMM's identity: a creator who could name the AMM program could name one they
wrote, owning a fake pool that points at token accounts they control, and
the "price" would be whatever balances they set. The deploy slot pins the
reviewed implementation, exactly as `PoolRef` does for admin markets.

fields.name: amm_kind
docs: `AmmKind` as a byte.

fields.name: enabled
docs: New markets may use this AMM. Existing markets keep their own pin and
are unaffected by this switch.

types.name: IsolatedConfig
docs: Protocol-wide policy for creator markets. Seeded `["isolated_config"]`.

fields.name: quote_mint
docs: The quote asset of every creator market: bridged SOL. Fixed at init.

fields.name: creation_fee
docs: Charged once, in quote base units, to `Global::fee_destination`.

fields.name: creation_enabled
docs: Admin switch for *new* markets only. Turning it off touches nothing that
already exists.

fields.name: next_market_id
docs: The id the next creator market will take. Starts at
`ISOLATED_MARKET_ID_BASE` and only increases.

fields.name: pending_amms
docs: A queued allowlist change and when it may be applied. `eta == 0` means
nothing is queued. Allowlist changes re-pin existing markets through
`sync_isolated_amm_pins`, so they wait out
`ISOLATED_ADMIN_TIMELOCK_SECONDS`.

types.name: IsolatedConfigArgs
docs: Everything the admin may set on `IsolatedConfig` after creation.

types.name: IsolatedMarket
docs: One creator market. Seeded `["isolated_market", market]`.

fields.name: creator
docs: Receives the creator fee and owns the bond. Has no other power.

fields.name: isolated_oracle
docs: The token oracle's observation history (`IsolatedOracle`).

fields.name: single_pool
docs: Both oracle slots name the same pool. Only the lowest tier allows it.

fields.name: bond_vault
docs: First-loss insurance for the quote reserve's lenders, in quote base
units, held in `bond_vault`. Idle by design: it must be there, in full,
at the moment a loan goes bad.

fields.name: bond_used
docs: Bond spent repaying loans that went bad. Never decreases.

fields.name: depth_borrow_cap
docs: Caps implied by measured pool depth, before the bond is considered.

fields.name: measured_quote_depth
docs: The depth they were computed from.

fields.name: creator_fee_hwm
docs: Share exchange rate at the last creator-fee harvest, 1e18-scaled. Fees
are charged only on gains above it, so a loss is recovered before the
creator earns again.

fields.name: creator_fee_shares
docs: Shares ever minted to the creator as fees.

fields.name: frozen
docs: Set by the admin. Stops new borrowing; nothing else.

fields.name: unfreeze_eta
docs: When a requested unfreeze may take effect. Freezing is instant;
unfreezing waits `ISOLATED_ADMIN_TIMELOCK_SECONDS`. Zero when none is
queued.

fields.name: retired
docs: Set by the creator, irreversibly. Stops new borrowing so the bond can be
released as loans close.

types.name: IsolatedOracle
docs: The observation history behind a creator market's token oracle.
# Why not `MarketOracle`
Admin markets keep `MarketOracle` and `refresh_market_oracle` exactly as
they are. Creator markets are thinner and their creator controls the pools,
so their oracle needs rules the admin path does not have (see
`refresh_isolated_oracle`). Two things follow from giving them their own
account type **at the same address** `MarketOracle` would occupy,
`["market_oracle", oracle]`:
- `refresh_market_oracle` and `set_market_oracle_config` cannot run against
a creator oracle: the account at that address does not deserialize as a
`MarketOracle`;
- `init_market_oracle` cannot attach a `MarketOracle` to one either: the
address is taken.
So the hardened refresh is the only way a creator oracle's price moves, with
no change to any existing instruction.

fields.name: oracle
docs: The `OracleState` this history feeds.

fields.name: config
docs: From the tier. Not changeable by anyone after creation.

fields.name: last_good_read
docs: The last time every pool read cleanly. Drives `cover_isolated_debt`'s
dead-oracle case; a degraded refresh does not move it.

fields.name: degraded_reads
docs: Refreshes that found a pool unreadable, in total. For monitoring.

fields.name: global
docs: The protocol instance this market belongs to.

fields.name: market_id
docs: Index this market's PDA is derived from (`["market", market_id]`). The
market is identified by this id, never by an individual's address.

fields.name: quote_currency_mint
docs: The mint every obligation value in this market is denominated in. For
Aera Core this is COOK itself, so a "value" in this program is a COOK
amount and the borrow reserve's own price is 1.0.

fields.name: name
docs: Human label, e.g. "Aera Core". Fixed width so the account size is known.

types.name: MarketOracle
docs: Verified observation history for one market-priced oracle.
Seeded `["market_oracle", oracle]`.

fields.name: oracle
docs: The `OracleState` this history belongs to.

fields.name: collateral_mint
docs: The collateral asset being priced, and the asset it is priced in.

fields.name: pools
docs: The two pools this oracle may read. Both must be healthy.

fields.name: next_index
docs: Where the next observation is written.

fields.name: pending_config
docs: A queued loosening and when it may be applied.

types.name: MarketOracleConfig
docs: Thresholds a market price must satisfy before it may back a loan.
Every one is configuration rather than a constant. Reusing bCOOK's breaker
bounds here would be wrong by orders of magnitude: those are 200 bps up and
100 bps down per *stake-pool epoch*, roughly 53 hours, and a memecoin moves
that much before lunch.
Thresholds only. The AMM each pool belongs to is identity and lives in
`PoolRef`, so this struct holds nothing that changes what is being priced --
only how strictly.

fields.name: twap_window_seconds
docs: Seconds the TWAP averages over.

fields.name: min_observations
docs: Observations required before borrowing may be enabled.

fields.name: min_span_seconds
docs: Seconds those observations must span. Ten samples in ten slots is one
sample, however many rows it writes.

fields.name: min_spacing_seconds
docs: Minimum gap between accepted observations, which is what stops a caller
filling the window from one short manipulation.

fields.name: max_observation_age_seconds
docs: Older than this and the reference stops being usable.

fields.name: warn_age_seconds
docs: Age at which the oracle warns before it freezes.

fields.name: max_cross_pool_deviation_bps
docs: Maximum tolerated disagreement between the two pools, in bps of their
midpoint. Live COOKHOUSE deviation was measured at ~88 bps, so this is
not a formality.

fields.name: min_pool_quote_depth
docs: Minimum quote-side depth per pool, in quote base units.

fields.name: max_rise_bps_per_window
docs: The most the reference may *rise* per TWAP window, in bps.
There is deliberately no downward equivalent. See
`OracleSourceKind::falls_are_always_accepted`.

types.name: Observation
docs: One verified reading. Every field is derived by the program.

fields.name: price
docs: Combined price, 1e18-scaled, in quote units per whole collateral token.

fields.name: slot
docs: From the `Clock` sysvar, never from the caller.

fields.name: quote_depth
docs: Total quote-side depth across both pools when this was taken.
Recorded so a later reader can tell whether a price was set against a
deep book or a thin one, which is the difference between a real move and
one somebody bought.

types.name: PoolRef
docs: The pools a market oracle may derive its price from.
Per-oracle, not global. A second Tier 3 market has its own pools, and generic
code must never carry one asset's addresses.
# Each pool pins its own AMM
The AMM identity used to live once in `MarketOracleConfig`, which forced
both pools onto the same program. That is the weaker arrangement: two pools
on one AMM share one upgrade key and one implementation, so a single bug or a
single compromised key moves both readings at once and the cross-pool
deviation check never fires.
Pinning per pool lets the two readings come from **different** AMMs with
different upgrade authorities -- Cookiebox's DAMM v2 and CookieSwap's CPAMM
are controlled by unrelated keys -- which is the point of having two pools at
all. Two pools on the same AMM remain allowed: both entries simply name it.
Identity, so immutable after `init_market_oracle`. Repointing a pool at a
different AMM is not a parameter change, it is a different oracle.

fields.name: collateral_vault
docs: The pool's vault for the collateral asset, as named by the pool account.

fields.name: quote_vault
docs: The pool's vault for the quote asset.

fields.name: amm_kind
docs: `AmmKind` as a byte. Selects the decoder.

fields.name: amm_program
docs: The AMM whose pool this is. Checked as the owner of the pool account.

fields.name: amm_program_data
docs: The AMM's `ProgramData`, and the deploy slot it stood at when configured.
The AMM is upgradeable by a key Aera does not control. Aera cannot stop
that; it can refuse to keep pricing against an implementation it has not
seen. Same mechanism as the stake-pool pin on `OracleState`.

fields.name: stale
docs: Set whenever deposits/borrows change; cleared by `refresh_obligation`.
Health-dependent handlers reject a stale obligation so they never act on
cached values a prior instruction in the same transaction invalidated.

fields.name: prices_stressed
docs: True when any feed this obligation depends on had its circuit breaker
latched at the last refresh — the collateral's feed as much as the
debt's. `borrow` refuses while this is set.
The flag lives here rather than being read straight from a feed because
`borrow` only carries the *borrowed* asset's feed in its accounts; the
collateral's feed is seen by `refresh_obligation` alone, and a 25% move
in the collateral is precisely the case worth stopping.

fields.name: deposited_value
docs: Σ every deposit's market value at face, FIXED_POINT_SCALE-scaled.
This is what the UI shows as "collateral value"; it is *not* what backs
the borrow limit — see `effective_collateral_value`.

fields.name: effective_collateral_value
docs: Σ every deposit's value *after* its haircut. This is the spec's
`collateral_value`, and the basis for both limits below.

fields.name: borrowed_value
docs: Σ every borrow's market value, FIXED_POINT_SCALE-scaled.

fields.name: allowed_borrow_value
docs: Σ (effective deposit value * reserve LTV). Borrows may not exceed this.

fields.name: unhealthy_borrow_value
docs: Σ (effective deposit value * reserve liquidation threshold). Above this
the obligation is liquidatable.

fields.name: market_value
docs: Face value, before haircut.

fields.name: borrowed_principal
docs: Principal scaled by the reserve's index at borrow time, so live debt
grows automatically as that index advances.

types.name: SupplyPosition
docs: Per-(reserve, wallet) record of how much liquidity this wallet has supplied
through the program. Exists solely to enforce `per_wallet_supply_cap`.
This tracks supply *through Aera*, not aCOOK held: a wallet that receives
aCOOK by transfer is not charged against its cap, and a wallet that sends
aCOOK away does not free cap until it withdraws. Nothing here can stop one
person using several wallets — the cap is a concentration brake on the
honest path, not a proof of identity, and PARAMS.md says so plainly.

fields.name: supplied_liquidity
docs: Net liquidity supplied: increased on supply, decreased on withdraw.

types.name: OracleState
docs: Everything Aera knows about one asset's price.

fields.name: market
docs: The market this serves. Part of the PDA seeds, so one market can never
write another's oracle.

fields.name: mint
docs: The asset being priced. For the native source this must equal the mint
the stake pool issues.

fields.name: source_kind
docs: Which source implementation reads this. [`OracleSourceKind`] as `u8`.

fields.name: source_program
docs: The program that must own `source_account`. Zero for
[`OracleSourceKind::UnitOfAccount`], which reads nothing.

fields.name: source_account
docs: The exact account the rate is derived from. Configuration, never
caller-supplied. Zero for `UnitOfAccount`.

fields.name: max_withdrawal_fee_bps
docs: Past this, an observation is refused and borrowing freezes. This is the
bound that stops the source's operator consuming Aera's risk margin by
raising their own redemption fee.

fields.name: rate_floor
docs: Absolute bounds on the gross rate, outside which the number cannot be a
rate for this asset at all. Not the circuit breaker — these catch a
redefined or corrupted field, the breaker catches movement.

fields.name: expected_deploy_slot
docs: The source program's deploy slot at configuration time.
Zero for [`OracleSourceKind::UnitOfAccount`], which reads no program.

fields.name: expected_upgrade_authority
docs: The source program's upgrade authority at configuration time, or all
zeros if it was already immutable.

fields.name: reference
docs: The last observation the breaker accepted. The protocol's anchor, and
the price liquidation falls back to during an incident.

fields.name: health
docs: Where in the state machine this oracle sits. [`OracleHealth`] as `u8`.

fields.name: last_moved_bps
docs: Movement of the last observation against the reference, in basis
points, whether or not it was accepted. Recorded so an operator can see
how close to a bound the source has been running.

fields.name: last_refresh_slot
docs: Slot of the last refresh *attempt*. Risk-changing instructions require
this to be the current slot, which is what makes a stale-price attack
have no path: the price must have been re-derived in this same
transaction.

fields.name: last_source_epoch
docs: The source's own freshness marker at the last attempt. For a stake pool
this is `last_update_epoch`, and it is recorded rather than enforced —
a stale pool understates bCOOK's value, which is the safe direction.

types.name: PendingConfig
docs: A queued loosening change. `eta == 0` means "nothing pending".

fields.name: eta
docs: Unix timestamp from which `apply_pending_params` may execute.

fields.name: liquidity_vault
docs: Program-owned token account holding un-borrowed liquidity. Its authority
is this reserve PDA.

fields.name: share_mint
docs: Share-token mint (aCOOK / abCOOK). Mint authority is this reserve PDA.

fields.name: oracle
docs: The [`OracleState`] this reserve prices from.
Renamed from `price_feed` in v0.2. Same offset, same width, so the
account layout is unchanged and existing reserves need no realloc --
migration repoints this at the new oracle account and closes the old
guardian feed.

fields.name: available_liquidity
docs: Base units sitting in `liquidity_vault`. This is the source of truth for
the pool size, not the vault's token balance, so a raw token donation
cannot move the exchange rate.

fields.name: share_mint_supply
docs: Outstanding share supply, mirrored here so valuations need only the
reserve account. A holder burning shares directly via the token program
makes the real supply drift below this mirror; that drift only lowers
what the burner could redeem, so the pool never pays out more than it
holds.

fields.name: borrowed_principal
docs: Total borrowed principal, scaled by the index at borrow time. Live debt
is `borrowed_principal * borrow_index / FIXED_POINT_SCALE`.

fields.name: borrow_index
docs: Monotonically increasing borrow index, FIXED_POINT_SCALE-scaled. Starts
at 1.0 and only ever multiplies by factors >= 1. This is the spec's
`variableBorrowIndex`.

fields.name: accrued_fees
docs: Interest owed to `Global::fee_destination`. Carved out of
`total_liquidity` so it never inflates the supplier exchange rate.

fields.name: pending
docs: A queued *loosening* config change, applied only after its timelock.

types.name: ReserveConfig
docs: Risk, interest and cap parameters. All ratios are basis points.

fields.name: loan_to_value_bps
docs: Fraction of (post-haircut) collateral value a borrower may draw.

fields.name: liquidation_threshold_bps
docs: Above this fraction the obligation may be liquidated.

fields.name: liquidation_bonus_bps
docs: Extra collateral a liquidator receives, as a fraction of value repaid.

fields.name: close_factor_bps
docs: Fraction of a borrow one liquidation may close while HF >= 0.95.

fields.name: collateral_haircut_bps
docs: Discount applied to this asset's collateral value before LTV and LT.
500 (5%) for bCOOK; 0 for an asset marked at face value.

fields.name: optimal_utilization_bps
docs: Utilization at which the borrow rate reaches `optimal_borrow_rate_bps`.

fields.name: min_borrow_rate_bps
docs: Borrow APR at 0% utilization.

fields.name: optimal_borrow_rate_bps
docs: Borrow APR at the kink.

fields.name: max_borrow_rate_bps
docs: Borrow APR at 100% utilization.

fields.name: reserve_factor_bps
docs: Share of interest kept by the protocol, all of it accruing to
`Global::fee_destination`. The rest lifts the supplier exchange rate.

fields.name: origination_fee_bps
docs: One-off fee charged when liquidity is drawn, in basis points of the
amount borrowed. Ships at 0 and is capped at
`MAX_ADMIN_ORIGINATION_FEE_BPS`.
The borrower owes the full amount and receives the amount minus this
fee, which is retained in the vault and recognised immediately as
protocol revenue. Suppliers' claim on the pool is unchanged by it — the
fee comes from the borrower, not from them.

fields.name: supply_cap
docs: Maximum liquidity the reserve will hold. 0 means "no cap".

fields.name: borrow_cap
docs: Maximum liquidity that may be borrowed out. 0 means "no cap".

fields.name: per_wallet_supply_cap
docs: Maximum a single wallet may supply. 0 means "no cap".

fields.name: borrow_enabled
docs: May liquidity be borrowed from this reserve?

fields.name: collateral_enabled
docs: May this reserve's share token be posted as collateral?

fields.name: isolated
docs: Isolated assets may only be paired with other isolated-compatible
collateral. Reserved for a second collateral listing; enforced in
`risk::check_isolation`.

fields.name: slots_per_year
docs: Slots in a year: the divisor turning the APR fields into a per-slot
rate. This is the cluster's slot time expressed as a count, so it is
configuration, not a constant — Cookie Chain's slot time can change, and
a stale value here charges borrowers at the wrong wall-clock rate while
every other number still reads correctly.

types.name: RiskConfig
docs: Risk limits for one reserve, added in v0.3.
Seeded `["risk_config", reserve]`. Created only for reserves that need one.

fields.name: reserve
docs: The reserve these limits apply to. Checked against the passed account.

fields.name: per_wallet_borrow_cap
docs: The most one wallet may owe in this reserve. `0` is unlimited.
Zero means unlimited to match every other cap in the protocol. Two caps
that meant opposite things by zero would be a configuration footgun of
exactly the kind found in production rather than in review.
## What this is, and what it is not
It is **not** Sybil resistance. One person can open a second wallet and
nothing here stops them. Any description of it as a per-person limit is
wrong.
It bounds the size of a *single liquidation*, which matters because
liquidator economics depend on how the seized collateral is sold.
Against COOKHOUSE's measured book, a liquidator routing across both
Meteora pools slips under 4% at every size the caps permit and profits
monotonically. One selling into the thinner pool alone slips 9.10% at
75,000 of debt closed, peaks in profit near 50,000, and is underwater
past roughly 90,000.
The cap is sized against the second case, because a liquidator with one
venue integrated is a liquidator who exists and the protocol does not
choose which kind turns up. A market-wide borrow cap does not stop one
borrower reaching that size alone. This does.
`tools/liquidation-economics.ts` computes both columns from the
observation log rather than from a figure copied forward.
The obligation PDA is `["obligation", market, owner]` opened with `init`,
so a wallet holds exactly one obligation per market and cannot split debt
across several to evade the check.

fields.name: protocol_liquidation_share_bps
docs: Aera's share of the liquidation bonus, in basis points of value repaid.
**Carved out of the existing bonus, never added to it.** With a 1200 bps
total bonus and this at 150, the borrower still loses exactly 12% and the
liquidator receives 10.5% instead of 12%. A borrower's penalty does not
depend on this field at all — `risk::split_seized_shares` divides an
already-computed seizure rather than enlarging it.
Zero means Aera takes nothing, which is Core's setting and the default
for a reserve with no `RiskConfig` at all. Bounded by
[`crate::constants::MAX_PROTOCOL_LIQUIDATION_SHARE_BPS`] and separately
by the collateral reserve's own `liquidation_bonus_bps`, since a share
larger than the bonus would take from the liquidator's principal.
Lives on the **collateral** reserve, beside the bonus it splits.
`liquidation_bonus_bps` is a property of the asset being seized, not of
the debt being repaid, and putting the two halves of one number in
different places would be a reliable source of misconfiguration.

fields.name: pending_per_wallet_borrow_cap
docs: A queued loosening, and when it may be applied.
Raising a cap is a loosening and waits out `Global::param_timelock_seconds`,
exactly as `ReserveConfig` loosenings do. Lowering one is a tightening and
lands immediately -- reducing what a wallet may owe can never make the
market less safe, and an operator responding to an incident should not
have to wait a day to do it.
`eta == 0` means nothing is queued.

fields.name: pending_protocol_liquidation_share_bps
docs: The queued share. Raising Aera's cut is a loosening and waits; lowering
it lands immediately, because a smaller protocol cut always leaves the
liquidator more and can never make the market less safe.
The amount written off, in the reserve's base units, at the index
current when it was recognised.
This event is the permanent record. There is no `Reserve::bad_debt`
field -- see the module docs for why -- so a reader wanting cumulative
bad debt sums these.
fields.name: amount

docs: The scaled principal removed from `Reserve::borrowed_principal`.
fields.name: principal_removed

docs: Which of the three cases applied.
fields.name: case

docs: Paid from the bond into the lenders' vault.
fields.name: covered

docs: Written off against lenders because the bond ran out. Zero unless the
coverage rule was overrun.
fields.name: written_off

docs: Collateral shares transferred to the creator.
fields.name: collateral_shares

docs: The reference after this refresh.
fields.name: reference

docs: The spot reading, before clamping. Zero on a degraded refresh.
fields.name: spot

docs: What was written to the history, after clamping. Zero if nothing was.
fields.name: recorded_price

docs: Emitted once per liquidation.
`seized_shares` keeps its meaning exactly -- everything taken from the
borrower -- so an existing consumer reading it still gets the borrower's
total penalty and needs no change. The four fields after it are additive,
and `liquidator_shares + protocol_shares == seized_shares` always holds.
types.name: Liquidated

docs: Everything removed from the borrower. Unchanged by the protocol share.
fields.name: seized_shares

docs: What the liquidator actually received.
fields.name: liquidator_shares

docs: What Aera received. Zero for Core, and zero whenever the share rounds
away on a small liquidation.
fields.name: protocol_shares

docs: The collateral reserve's total bonus, for context on the split.
fields.name: total_bonus_bps

docs: The configured share, before rounding. `protocol_shares` may be zero
while this is not.
fields.name: protocol_share_bps

docs: The combined price recorded, which is the lower of the two pools.
fields.name: price

docs: The time-weighted reference after this observation.
fields.name: reference

docs: The health the oracle is in after this observation.
fields.name: health

docs: A rise was admitted only as far as the configured bound.
fields.name: rise_capped

docs: Whether this refresh appended to the observation history, or only
re-priced and restated freshness because it fell inside the spacing
window. A keeper uses this to tell a useful crank from a no-op.
fields.name: recorded
